sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 /
CR / 26 / 2013-14 dated 06.04.2021 in respect of Sy. No.108 measuring 2195.04 Sq. feet of Yelahanka village and Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District.

. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property bearing Sy. No.108 measuring 2195.04 Sq. feet situated at Yelahanka village and Hobli has been acquired under Gazette notification No. S.O. No.1874(E) dated 30.07.2010.
Prior to that Preliminary Notification issued under S.O. No.3159(E) dated 09.12.2009.
Subsequently the respondent No.2/LAO has awarded a total sum of Rs.30,48,910/- as compensation for 2195.04 Sq. feet of the land belongs to the petitioner.
The petitioner received the same under protest and filed an application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Sq. feet as on 25.06.2013.
Accordingly, the said application taken by the respondent No. 3 for consideration.
.3. In the said petition, the respondent No.2 filed statement of objection stating that the contention urged by the petitioner are baseless and the same are made without any substance.
The petitioner has not produced any relevant documents to justify his claim for A.P. No.89/2022 enhanced compensation and the claim of the petitioner cannot be sustained in law.
Hence, question of enhancement of compensation will not arise and the claim of the petitioner is liable to be dismissed by the respondent No.2.
Accordingly, prayed to dismiss the reference.

.4. Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB /
NH-7/CR-20(A) / 2013-14, 79/2012-13, 26/2013-14, 88/2012-13, 9/2012-13 dated 06.04.2021.
.5.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :
:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claim that the impugned award passed by the respondent No.3 is wholly erroneous, contrary to law, materials on records and in violation of Principles Gopalappa Y M vs The Project Director And General ... on 2 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147285556/
2 of natural justice and the same is liable to be set aside.

sentences.text: The petitioner claim that the respondent No.3 committed a legal A.P. No.89/2022 misconduct in not following the documents filed by the petitioner for deciding the market value.
The Arbitrator failed to appreciate the fact that the respondent No. 3 has not produced any documents to justify the award passed by him.
The award dated 02.04.2011 passed by the respondent No. 2 is not in accordance with the guidance value under Section 3G(7) of NH Act.
The award amount is not at all matching with the market value for prime land of the petitioner.

The land acquired is more than value than the award amount,
even the amount awarded.
The respondent No. 3 enhanced just and meager compensation without taken into consideration material evidence placed before the Court, which is against probabilities of the case.

That due to land acquired by the respondents, the petitioner lost his land and the adjacent land owners of the same village have got a high value for their property, hence, this Court has to reconsider the claim of grossly erred in considering the fact that the acquired land situated very near to Bengaluru International Airport and situated midst of the lands commercially developed.

The LAO and Arbitrator has not recorded any evidence and not considered for payment of solatium on the award amount and additional market A.P.
No.89/2022 value along with interest from the date of taking possession till the date of payment.
Accordingly, prayed for reconsidering the impugned award and also alternative prayer to remand the matter to the Arbitrator for fresh consideration.

.6. The respondents 1 and 2 filed a detailed objections claiming that the application is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the respondent No. 3 passed the award as per the guidance value produced before the Arbitrator pertaining to the year 2011.
The petitioner is attempting to mislead this Court by drawing reference to incorrect/wholly inapplicable guidance notification.
The respondent No.1 totally denied all the grounds claimed by the petitioner in the petition.

The Arbitrator/ respondent No. 3 passed the award after giving full opportunity of hearing to the petitioners by considering the material evidence on record for enhancement of compensation together with all other statutory benefits available under A.P. No.89/2022 the LA Act in accordance with law and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
.7. The petitioner along with the petition filed I.A. No. 1 under Section 34(3) of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, for condonation of delay if any filing the petition.

.8. The above application is supported with the affidavit of petitioner, wherein, it is stated that the order has not been communicated to him and when he approached the concerned authority on 04.03.2022, he came to know about the order and he immediately applied for copy of the order and he got the same on 26.05.2022.
Thereafter, filed this petition and accordingly prayed for condonation of delay if any in filing the petition.
.9. The respondent No.1 has not filed any objections to the IA.
.10. The respondents No.1 and 2 appeared before the Court through their Advocate.

The respondent N o . 3 a p p e a r e d t h r o u g h D G P . T h e e n t i r e r e c o r d s i n A . P . N o . 8 9 / 2 0 2 2 Gopalappa Y M vs The Project Director And General ... on 2 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147285556/
3 LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/26/2013-14 secured from the Arbitrator.
.11.

On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
1) Whether the petition filed by the petitioner is within time ?
2) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
3) What order or award?
.12.
Heard the arguments.

sentences.text:
Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Points No.1 & 2 : In the affirmative Point No.3 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .13. POINT NO.1: Perused the I.A. No.1 along with affidavit that has been filed for condonation of delay in filing the petition, satisfied with reasons therein and the said application is not opposed by the respondent No. 1.
Accordingly, I am of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to condone the delay in filing the petition.
Accordingly the point No. 1 is answered in the affirmative.
.14. POINT No.2:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note an admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The petitioner Sri. Y.M. Gopalappa is A.P. No.89/2022 an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.108 measuring to an extent of 2195.04 Sq. feet of Yelahanka village and Hobli, Bengaluru North Additional Taluka and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 30.07.2010,
that has been published in the official Gazette on 30.07.2010, is an admitted fact.
It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.30,48,910/- being the land value was disbursed to the petitioner as compensation.

.15. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the petitioner Sri. Y.M.
Gopalappa filed an application before the respondent No.3 claiming that he is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Sq. feet as on 25.06.2013

On basis of the said application, the respondent No.3 hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH- Gopalappa Y M vs The Project Director And General ... on 2 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147285556/

sentences.text:
The respondent No.3 in its order enhanced the A.P. No.89/2022 compensation at Rs.3,000/- per Sq.
feet from Rs. 1,389/- per Sq. feet and awarded additional compensation of Rs. 1,611/- per Sq. feet.
.16.
The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.3 without considering the documentary evidence placed by the petitioner and also without considering the claim of the petitioner that other properties have enhanced the market value which is much higher than the compensation enhanced by the respondent No. 3.
The said claim of the petitioner is also found in the award.

On close perusal of the order passed by the respondent No. 3, it is clear that the respondent No. 3 considering the guidance value of the year 2010-11 published vide notification bearing No. CVC 19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011 enhanced the compensation, but there is no material on record to show that the petitioner has produced the alleged documents claimed by the A.P. No.89/2022 petitioner in the petition for perusal of Arbitrator/respondent No. 3.
.17.

However, it is the definite case of petitioner that the very same Arbitrator in different cases has enhanced the market value 3 times and such enhancement of compensation not given to the claimant though the property of the petitioner is acquired for National Highways and the said property of the petitioner was abutting to the National Highways.

.18. In support of this contention, the petitioner has produced the copy of the order passed in LAQ/ARB/NH-07/CR/01/2019-20 has enhanced the compensation 3 times of the compensation awarded by LAO/ respondent No. 2.

Admittedly in the case on hand, the LAO awarded the compensation of Rs.1,389/- per Sq. feet and it is enhanced to the tune of Rs.3,000/- per Sq. feet by enhancing only Rs.1611/- per Sq. feet as per table in the award.
Therefore, the claim of the petitioner is probable that the respondent No.3 has not properly appreciated the material placed before him while A.P. No.89/2022 passing the order.
Apart from that, the impugned order of the respondent No. 3 also does not disclose any reasons for the enhancement made in the impugned award.

The Arbitrator has stated much about contention taken by petitioner and respondent No. 1 in the order and abruptly decided the market value without assigning any proper reasons particularly in this case why the petitioner is not entitled for enhancement of three times as enhanced in other cases.

Hence,
the order of the LAO certainly liable to be intervened by this court.
Accordingly, the point No.2 is held in the affirmative.
.19. Point No.3:
In view of my above findings, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER IA filed by the petitioner to condone the delay in filing the petition is allowed.
Petition filed under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is hereby allowed.

Consequently, the impugned award passed by the respondent No.3 in case LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/26/2013-14 dated 06.04.2021 in respect of Sy. No.108 measuring 2195.04 Sq.
feet of Yelahanka village and Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District is set aside with liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
